text:
Ordinary Maxwell theory includes:

\[
\nabla\cdot \mathbf B=0,
\qquad
\nabla\times \mathbf E=-\frac{\partial \mathbf B}{\partial t}.
\]

If magnetic charges exist, Gauss’s law for magnetism becomes

\[
\nabla\cdot \mathbf B \propto \rho_m.
\]

A moving magnetic charge produces a magnetic current \(\mathbf J_m\). Charge conservation then requires Faraday’s law to acquire an extra term:

\[
\nabla\times \mathbf E=-\frac{\partial \mathbf B}{\partial t}-\mathbf J_m
\]

(up to unit-dependent constants). Therefore both the divergence of the magnetic field and the circulation (curl) of the electric field change—not merely \(\nabla\cdot\mathbf B\).

Answer: B
